events.region: Boone, IN; Clinton, IN; Fountain, IN; Montgomery, IN; Parke, IN; Tippecanoe, IN; Vermillion, IN
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWIND

The National Weather Service in Indianapolis has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northwestern Boone County in central Indiana...
Southwestern Clinton County in central Indiana...
Fountain County in west central Indiana...
Montgomery County in west central Indiana...
Northern Parke County in west central Indiana...
Southeastern Tippecanoe County in west central Indiana...
Northwestern Vermillion County in west central Indiana...

* Until 830 AM EDT.

* At 337 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 0.5 and 2 inches of
rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses as well as
other poor drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Crawfordsville, Veedersburg, Thorntown, Cayuga, Waynetown,
Darlington, Linden, Colfax, New Market, Clarks Hill, Hillsboro,
Kingman, Perrysville, Waveland, New Richmond, Wingate, Mellott,
Wallace, Alamo and Shades State Park.

This includes the following highways...
Interstate 65 between mile markers 145 and 164.
Interstate 74 between mile markers 11 and 44.

State Recreation Area, and Middle Fork State Fish and Wildlife Area.

thunderstorms producing heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2
and 6 inches of rain have fallen, with the highest amounts near

drainage ditches, low-lying areas, and poor drainage areas.
Widespread street and underpass flooding. Possible flooding
of structures, including basements. Possible flooding of
highways.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Paxton, Gibson City, Cissna Park, Buckley, Melvin, Loda, Roberts,
Elliott, Sibley, Clarence and Claytonville.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Southeastern Livingston County in central Illinois...
North Central Ford County in east central Illinois...
Iroquois County in east central Illinois...

* WHEN...Until 415 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Roads and
streets may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 226 AM CDT, Doppler radar indicated the heaviest rainfall was
ending. Automated rain gauges indicate that up to 3.5 inches of
rain has fallen over the last 3 to 4 hours. Minor flooding is
likely ongoing across parts of the advisory area, particularly
from Fairbury to Watseka and points southward.
- Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are expected over
the area.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Watseka, Fairbury, Gilman, Clifton, Milford, Chatsworth, Onarga,
Forrest, Sheldon, Chebanse, Piper City, Ashkum, Cullom, Saunemin,
Martinton, Crescent City, Danforth, Beaverville and Woodland.

events.region: Kaibab Plateau; Marble and Glen Canyons; Grand Canyon Country
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Grand Canyon, Kaibab Plateau, Marble and Glen Canyons.

* WHEN...From 11 AM MST  /noon MDT/ this morning through this
evening.

* IMPACTS...Flash flooding will be possible in creeks, normally dry
washes, swimming holes, and over recently burned areas. Raging
killer currents will be possible in side canyons and narrow slot
canyons. Low-water crossings may be flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Thunderstorms are expected to develop this afternoon and continue
into the early evening hours across northwestern Arizona. With
deep monsoonal moisture in place, any stronger storm will have
the potential to produce heavy rainfall and cause flash flooding.
- Some locations that may experience flooding include...
Page area Slot Canyons, Supai, and the Grand Canyon National Park
downstream of the Dragon Bravo Fire scar.
- Additional information is available at weather.gov/flagstaff.
